CHAPTER 2

Reading Code
阅读代码

Code is read much more often than it is written.
——Guido van Rossum, creator of Python

代码被阅读的次数，远远多于被编写的次数。
——Guido van Rossum，Python 之父

Despite the way coding is taught, software engineers spend far more time reading code than writing it. In most beginner coding courses, you jump immediately into writing code, focusing on core language concepts and idioms without acknowledging that you’d never learn Polish or Portuguese in a similar manner. And while most academic projects start from a blank slate, practicing developers are almost always working within the confines of code that has taken years to arrive at its current state, something you can explore in depth in Chapter 6.

不管编程是怎么被教的，软件工程师花在阅读代码上的时间，远多于写代码。在大多数入门编程课上，你一上来就动手写代码，聚焦于语言核心概念和惯用法，却没人指出：你绝不会用同样的方式去学波兰语或葡萄牙语。而且，虽然大多数学术项目都从一张白纸开始，但在岗开发者几乎总是在一段已经积累了多年的代码里工作——这一点你会在第 6 章深入探讨。

With the advent of agentic or chat-oriented programming,1 reading code will become even more important for software engineers. While it may not be your first choice, you will work with code you did not write. Take heart, there are techniques to help you orient yourself when you encounter unfamiliar code. This chapter will go over why reading code can be challenging, and we’ll give some tips to make the process simpler.

随着智能体式或对话式编程1的兴起，阅读代码对软件工程师会变得更加重要。尽管这可能不是你的首选，但你终将与不是自己写的代码打交道。别担心，当你遇到不熟悉的代码时，有一些技巧可以帮你定位方向。本章会讲清楚为什么读代码有挑战，并给出一些让过程更轻松的窍门。

1 Sometimes known as vibe coding.
有时也被称为氛围编程（vibe coding）。

The Challenge of Working with Existing Code

Regardless of how you learned to code, you probably spent much of your time in the blissful space known as greenfield development, where you experience the joy of starting from scratch, unencumbered by the baggage of prior work. Yet, in your professional life, you’ve likely had vanishingly few opportunities to build an application from a blank editor. As a practicing software engineer, much of your time will be spent on brownfield development, working within the limits of an existing codebase day in and day out with legacy code.

不管你是怎么学会写代码的，你大概大部分时间都待在一个叫做“绿地开发”的幸福空间里：从零开始，没有历史包袱。然而在职场中，你能从空白编辑器开始搭建应用的机会少之又少。作为在岗软件工程师，你的大部分时间将花在“棕地开发”上——日复一日地在既有代码库的局限里，与遗留代码打交道。

原书第 39 页

Legacy Code by Any Other Name…
换个名字的遗留代码……

Reading old code is often a task most developers prefer to avoid. We often use the term legacy code to describe it, and this term is rarely meant as a compliment. There are any number of definitions of legacy code: code that was written yesterday, code without adequate test coverage or too much, or just code you didn’t write. However, you shouldn’t disparage the success of an existing application. If a product has delivered business value for years and has justified continued investment, that is worthy of a pat on the back. We prefer a more positive frame, such as heritage code or existing code. For a more in-depth discussion of the topic, see Chapter 6.
阅读老代码往往是大多数开发者避之不及的活儿。我们常用“遗留代码”（legacy code）来称呼它，而这个词很少带有褒义。对遗留代码的定义五花八门：昨天刚写的代码、测试覆盖不足（或过多）的代码，或者干脆就是“不是你写的代码”。然而，你不该贬低一个现有应用所取得的成功。如果一个产品多年来持续交付业务价值、证明了值得继续投入，那它就值得被肯定。我们更倾向于用一个更积极的说法，比如“传承代码”（heritage code）或“既有代码”。这个话题的深入讨论见第 6 章。

When asked to solve a problem that has to do with existing code, you actually have four problems to solve.

当你被要求解决一个与既有代码相关的问题时，你实际上要解决四个问题。

First and foremost, you need to understand the business problem you are trying to solve. And the domains that developers work in are very demanding! Software is eating the world, meaning software engineers are tasked with increasingly more complex business challenges; much of the proverbial low-hanging fruit has already been picked.

首先也是最重要的，你需要理解自己要解决的业务问题。而开发者所处的业务领域要求极高！软件正在吞噬世界，意味着软件工程师要应对越来越复杂的业务挑战；谚语中说的那种“低垂的果实”，大多已经被摘完了。

Second, you must see the problem through the eyes of the developer who came before you, and that is often the most challenging aspect of software development. Different developers solve problems in different ways; everyone has their habits and tendencies. Perhaps your predecessor had a predilection for a more functional style of programming that you aren’t as familiar with. Maybe they used a pattern that is new to you or leveraged a library that you haven’t used before. Whether you agree with the approach taken or not, there are many ways to solve a given problem.

其次，你必须从前一位开发者的视角去看这个问题，而这往往是软件开发中最有挑战的部分。不同的人用不同的方式解决问题；每个人都有自己的习惯和倾向。也许你的前任偏爱一种你不太熟悉的函数式编程风格；也许他用了一个你没见过的模式，或者用了一个你没用过的库。无论你是否认同他采取的方式，解决一个问题本就有很多条路。

Third, it’s possible the existing code doesn’t have the right level of abstraction. Perhaps it is modeled in a way that is too generic or fails to capture the proper nuance of the domain. Maybe the previous developer conflated two concepts or forced a favored pattern when another would have been more appropriate. Regardless, a larger refactoring may be required to make the code more understandable.

第三，既有代码的抽象层级可能并不恰当。也许它建模得过于泛化，没能抓住领域应有的细微差别；也许前任把两个概念混为一谈，或者硬塞了一个自己偏爱的模式，而换另一个模式本会更合适。无论如何，可能需要一次较大的重构才能让代码更易理解。

Fourth, much like an archaeologist, you are often peeling back layer after layer of technical debt, old technologies and approaches that may now be considered anti-patterns. Over time, languages and best practices evolve,2 and you will have to see the code through the lens of when it was written. You may even be able to “carbon date” the code simply by noticing what frameworks or language features are (or are not) used! Frameworks like Spring have evolved over the course of many years, often supporting multiple approaches to a given problem. What is considered the “right” way to do something changes over time.

第四，你常常像考古学家一样，一层一层剥开技术债、旧技术和如今可能被视为反模式的老做法。随着时间推移，语言和最佳实践不断演进，2你必须透过代码被写下时的那个时代的镜头去看它。你甚至只要留意代码用了（或没用）哪些框架和语言特性，就能给代码“碳定年”！像 Spring 这样的框架历经多年演进，往往对同一个问题支持多种做法。而什么才算“正确”的做法，是随时间变化的。

2 Or as Neal Ford once said: “Today’s best practice is tomorrow’s anti-pattern.”
或者正如 Neal Ford 曾说：“今天的最佳实践，就是明天的反模式。”
原书第 40 页

It also doesn’t help that you almost always have to deal with patches on top of patches. Maybe the last developer didn’t have a full understanding of the problem, or they weren’t up to speed on some new language feature that could greatly simplify the job at hand. Maybe the last developer had a premium license to an AI coding assistant and generated 20,000 lines of code per day. Add in the typical demands of fix-it-fast, and you could spend an afternoon deciphering a single method.

更糟的是，你几乎总是要面对“补丁摞补丁”的局面。也许上一个开发者并没有完全理解问题，或者他不了解某个本可以大幅简化手头工作的新语言特性；也许上一个开发者有 AI 编码助手的高级订阅、一天生成两万行代码。再加上“赶紧修好”的典型要求，你可能花一下午都读不懂一个方法。

Working with existing code presents technical challenges, making it understandable why it’s often one of a developer’s least favorite tasks. However, the aversion extends beyond technical issues to include cognitive biases as well.

与既有代码打交道充满技术挑战，难怪它常常是开发者最不喜欢的任务之一。然而，这种抵触不止于技术问题，还涉及认知偏见。

Cognitive Biases

When reading existing code, you might compare it unfavorably to your own work. Of course, you don’t write bad code, do you? On more than one occasion, we, your humble authors, have struggled with some code, uttering less polite variations of “What idiot wrote this?” only to discover that it was written by none other than ourselves. And frankly, if you read code you wrote a few years ago, you should be a little disappointed—that’s a sign of growth; you know more today than you did then. That is a good thing!

阅读既有代码时，你可能会拿它和自己的工作做不利的比较。当然，你自己可不会写糟糕的代码，对吧？我们这两位谦逊的作者，就不止一次对着某段代码抓破头，嘴里蹦出“这是哪个白痴写的”的不雅版本，结果发现作者正是自己。坦白说，如果你读到几年前自己写的代码，应该感到一点点失望——那正是成长的标志；你今天比那时懂得更多了。这是好事！

You also have a couple of cognitive biases working against you when you work with existing code. First is the IKEA effect, which is when you place a higher value on things you create. One study found people would pay 63% more for a product they successfully assembled themselves versus the identical product put together by someone else.3 If you’ve ever gone to a pick-your-own apple orchard, you are often charged a premium to, well, do some of the work yourself. You’ll do it, however, for the experience and the chance to select the very best fruit right off the trees. In software, developers often have strong opinions about the “right” way to do things and tend to prefer their own code and approach.

与既有代码打交道时，还有几种认知偏见在拖你的后腿。第一个是宜家效应：你会高估自己亲手创造的东西。一项研究发现，人们愿意为自己成功组装的产品多付 63% 的钱，而同样的产品由别人组装则不值这个价。3如果你去过自助采摘苹果园，就会知道：你往往要多付钱，只为了自己动手摘。但你还是会去，为了那份体验，为了能亲手从树上挑最好的果子。在软件领域，开发者往往对“正确”做法有强烈主张，倾向于偏爱自己的代码和方式。

3 Michael I. Norton, Daniel Mochon, and Dan Ariely, “The ‘IKEA Effect’: When Labor Leads to Love,” HBS Working Paper, No. 11-091 (2011).
Michael I. Norton、Daniel Mochon、Dan Ariely，《宜家效应：当劳动催生热爱》，哈佛商学院工作论文 No. 11-091（2011）。

Additionally, there is the mere-exposure effect: you tend to prefer the things you are already familiar with. This leads to the typical dogmatism many developers have around programming languages. Developers tend to think time began with whatever language they learned first. When Java first introduced Lambda expressions, someone on a language-specific mailing list asked why Java needed these “new-fangled Lambdas,” not realizing Lambdas are not a new concept in programming languages and were part of the original plan for Java itself!

此外还有多看效应：你会偏爱自己已经熟悉的东西。这导致许多开发者对编程语言抱有一种典型的教条主义。开发者往往觉得，时间是从自己学的第一门语言开始的。Java 刚引入 Lambda 表达式时，某个语言邮件列表上有人问：Java 为什么需要这些“新奇玩意儿 Lambda”？他没意识到，Lambda 在编程语言里并不是新概念，它本来就是 Java 最初设计的一部分！

原书第 41 页

Developers can be provincial around their preferred tools, which is something Paul Graham touches on in his essay “Beating the Averages”. Graham says programming languages exist on a power continuum, but you often can’t recognize why a language is more powerful than another. To demonstrate his point, he introduced the hypothetical Blub language and a productive Blub programmer. When the Blub programmer looks down the power continuum, all they see are languages that lack features they use every day, and they can’t understand why anyone would choose such an inferior tool. When they look up the power continuum, all they see are a bunch of weird features they don’t have in Blub, and they can’t imagine why anyone would need those to be productive since they aren’t in Blub.

开发者对自己偏爱的工具可能会很狭隘，Paul Graham 在他的文章《与平均值抗衡》里谈到了这一点。Graham 说，编程语言存在于一条能力连续谱上，但你往往看不出为什么某门语言比另一门更强。为说明这一点，他虚构了一门叫 Blub 的语言，以及一位高效的 Blub 程序员。当这位 Blub 程序员沿着能力谱往下看，看到的全是“缺少自己日常所用特性”的语言，他无法理解为什么有人会选这么差劲的工具；当他沿着能力谱往上看，看到的全是一堆 Blub 里没有的古怪特性，他又无法想象为什么有人会需要那些东西才能高效——反正 Blub 里没有。

As you work with code, as well as with your fellow developers, keep these biases in mind. If you aren’t sure why a colleague is so adamant about a certain tool or approach, ask if it might be an instance of the IKEA effect or the Blub paradox. Of course, you should also reflect on your own assumptions to ensure you aren’t exhibiting one of the predispositions yourself.

当你与代码、与同事打交道时，请把这些偏见记在心里。如果你不确定某位同事为什么对某个工具或方式如此固执，可以想想这会不会是宜家效应或 Blub 悖论在起作用。当然，你也应当反思自己的预设，确保自己没有也在犯这类毛病。

Approaching Unfamiliar Code

As much as you may wish you could spend all your work hours focused on crafting new code, you will encounter existing codebases throughout your career. How can you get up to speed on a new project without losing your mind? First, start with your teammates. A basic project overview should be part of any onboarding experience. Spend some time with the documentation. Many projects have a README file that will help you get your bearings, while others have wikis or websites designed to give you a concise overview.4 Projects may also have architecture decision records (ADRs).5 ADRs provide invaluable context and the all-important “why” that often vanishes in the rush of the latest defect or outage. You could learn more in a few minutes with the docs than in hours with the debugger. Reading the project’s coding standards will prepare you for the patterns you will encounter as you wade through the codebase.

尽管你可能希望把所有工时都花在打磨新代码上，但职业生涯中你总会遇到既有的代码库。怎样才能在不崩溃的情况下快速上手一个新项目？首先，从队友开始。任何入职流程都应包含一个基本的项目概览。再花点时间看看文档。许多项目有 README 帮你摸清方向，另一些则有 wiki 或网站给你一份简明概览。4项目还可能有架构决策记录（ADR）。5ADR 提供了无比宝贵的上下文，以及那个在赶工修最新缺陷或故障时往往被遗忘的、至关重要的“为什么”。看文档几分钟，可能比对着调试器几小时收获还多。读一遍项目的编码规范，能让你在蹚代码库时对即将遇到的模式有所准备。

4 Said documentation may be out-of-date, trust but verify.
这些文档可能已过时，信任但要核实。
5 To learn more about ADRs, see Chapter 3 of Head First Software Architecture by Raju Gandhi et al. (O’Reilly, 2024).
想了解 ADR，见 Raju Gandhi 等著《Head First 软件架构》第 3 章（O’Reilly，2024）。
原书第 42 页

If the documentation for the code you’re reading is out-of-date, update it as you learn; if it is nonexistent, consider building your own as you go. Apply the Golden Rule (discussed in Chapter 1). Creating the documentation will help you learn the project, and it will also serve the developers who come after you.

如果你正在读的代码的文档已过时，就在学习的过程中顺手更新；如果根本没有文档，就考虑边做边建。践行那条金科玉律（见第 1 章）。写文档既能帮你自己学懂项目，也能服务于后来的开发者。

There are any number of things you could document. As you read, write your documentation to favor lightweight, low-ceremony approaches seeking to answer common questions such as these:

你可以记录的东西很多。阅读时，用轻量、低仪式感的方式写文档，力求回答这些常见问题：

  • What does your service do?你的服务是做什么的？
  • How does it work?它是怎么工作的？
  • What does it depend on?它依赖什么？
  • How do you run the application?怎么启动这个应用？

Wait, we can hear you now: documentation may be (and often is) out of sync with the code. But believe us, that doesn’t have to be the case. Documentation can evolve with the code. The best way to ensure that it does is to use tests as documentation. Tests written with behavior-driven styles, if written properly, can produce executable documentation, a topic discussed at greater length in Chapter 5.

等等，我们现在就能听到你的嘀咕：文档可能（而且常常）和代码不同步。但相信我们，情况未必非得如此。文档可以与代码一同演进。确保这一点的最好办法，就是把测试当作文档。用行为驱动风格写的测试，如果写得好，可以产出可执行的文档——这个话题在第 5 章会详细展开。

Metrics Can Mislead
指标会误导人

Code coverage (how much of the codebase is executed when the tests are run) can be a useful metric on a project. However, there are no silver bullets in software, and it is possible to fail even with 100% code coverage. A friend of ours joined a project that was having regressions with every release. As he was getting up to speed on the code, he asked the tech lead if there were any tests. The tech lead proudly said, “Yes, we have right around 92% code coverage.” Impressed, our friend was somewhat surprised they had so many regressions, but he continued his analysis.
代码覆盖率（运行测试时执行了代码库中多大比例的代码）在项目里可以是一个有用的指标。然而软件没有银弹，即使 100% 覆盖率也可能照样出问题。我们的一个朋友加入了一个项目，那个项目每次发版都有回归 bug。他刚上手读代码时问技术主管有没有测试。主管骄傲地说：“有，我们差不多有 92% 的代码覆盖率。”朋友吃了一惊，但既然覆盖率这么高，怎么还有这么多回归？他继续分析下去。
Looking at the test code, he found some startling patterns. At first, he thought these were isolated, but eventually he discovered they were endemic to the codebase. He went back to the tech lead and said, “I couldn’t help but notice your tests don’t have any asserts.” The tech lead responded by repeating the code coverage statistic. The meta lesson is: be wary of any metric, because they can mislead. But don’t lose sight of the value and purpose of a practice. If it is just about ceremony, you are unlikely to get the benefit you expect. Project teams should regularly challenge themselves and their approach; don’t be afraid to change course when warranted.
看了测试代码，他发现了一些惊人的模式。起初他以为是个别现象，最后却发现整个代码库都这样。他回去找主管说：“我忍不住注意到，你们的测试里一个断言都没有。”主管的回应是——又重复了一遍代码覆盖率数字。这个元教训是：对任何指标都要保持警惕，因为它们会误导人。但也不要因此忘掉一项实践的价值和目的。如果只剩仪式感，你就别指望得到期望的收益。项目团队应当定期审视自己和自己的做法；该转向时别害怕。

Software Archeology

Once you’ve surveyed the team and familiarized yourself with any existing documentation, it is time to open your editor of choice and practice some software archeology. Roll up your sleeves and root around in the codebase! To paraphrase Sir Isaac Newton, look for smoother pebbles and prettier shells. Look at the code structure—how is the code organized? Some languages have first-class constructs for packaging code; others rely on conventions. How does the code fit together? Is this a monolith or a distributed architecture with dozens or hundreds of services? What domain concepts are expressed in the code? Read the tests—what do they tell you about the functionality? With that information, do you understand the intent of this class?

一旦你和团队聊过、也熟悉了现有文档，就该打开你最爱的编辑器，来做点软件考古了。卷起袖子，在代码库里刨一刨！套用牛顿的话：去寻找更光滑的卵石和更漂亮的贝壳。看看代码结构——代码是怎么组织的？有些语言有一等的打包结构，另一些则靠约定。代码是怎么拼装到一起的？是单体应用，还是有几十上百个服务的分布式架构？代码里表达了哪些领域概念？读读测试——它们告诉你哪些功能？有了这些信息，你理解这个类的意图了吗？

If the intent isn’t clear, dig further. Modern editors can make it trivially simple to see who calls a given function, allowing you to work your way backward. Callers should help you determine what a given class does and how it is used. Your backtracking may take you all the way to a service endpoint like an HTTP call, but eventually you should find the connection between a given user action and the code.

如果意图还不清楚，就继续往下挖。现代编辑器能让你极其轻松地看到谁调用了某个函数，从而让你反向追溯。调用者应当能帮你判断某个类是做什么的、又是怎么被使用的。你的反向追溯可能一路追到像 HTTP 调用这样的服务端点，但最终你应当能找到某个用户操作与代码之间的联系。

Once you have your bearings, run the application. What does it do? Find a specific element, be it something on a user interface or a parameter to a service call, and map that back to the code. Look at the issue list; see if focusing on a single feature or bug allows you to follow the coding path. Hunt for a landmark; if you know a given action results in an update to the datastore, find that in the code. Use your debugger to walk through the code—did it work the way you anticipated? Did you end up on a vastly different code path? Ultimately, you are building a mental model of the code; you are loading the application into your brain.

一旦有了方向感，就把应用跑起来。它是做什么的？找一个具体元素——不管是用户界面上的某个东西，还是某个服务调用的参数——把它映射回代码。看看 issue 列表；试着聚焦在单个功能或 bug 上，看能不能顺着编码路径走通。找一个地标：如果你知道某个操作会更新数据存储，就在代码里找到它。用调试器单步走一遍——它的行为和你预期的一样吗？你最终走到了一条完全不同的代码路径上吗？归根结底，你是在建立代码的心智模型；你在把这个应用装进自己的大脑。

What might this look like in practice? Let’s use the Spring PetClinic app as an example. Even if you aren’t an expert in Java or Spring, navigating the app should be fairly straightforward, plus it has excellent documentation. Once you’ve cloned and run the application, you’ll see that it has the ability to search for owners (see Figure 2-1). If you explore the owner templates, you’ll see one helpfully named findOwners.html,6 which references an /owners endpoint. Searching the project for /owners returns ample results, but a little intuition might lead you to the @GetMapping("/owners") annotation on the processFindForm method in the OwnerController file.

实际操作起来是什么样？我们以 Spring PetClinic 应用为例。即便你不是 Java 或 Spring 专家，导航这个应用也应该相当直观，而且它有极好的文档。克隆并运行应用后，你会看到它可以搜索主人（owner）（见图 2-1）。如果你翻一翻 owner 相关模板，会看到一个命名友好的 findOwners.html6，它引用了 /owners 端点。在项目里搜 /owners 会出来一大堆结果，但凭一点直觉，你可能会定位到 OwnerController 文件里 processFindForm 方法上的 @GetMapping("/owners") 注解。

Repeat the previous steps. Eventually, you will make the connection, allowing you to walk your way through the code and build your understanding as you go.

打个断点，从浏览器执行搜索，看看会发生什么！果然，你的调试器看起来应该类似图 2-2。如果直觉错了呢？重复前面的步骤。最终你会建立起联系，从而能一路走通代码，边走边建立理解。

Use your integrated development environment (IDE) to navigate the code. Many IDEs make it easy to jump to methods in other classes (see Figure 2-3) as you work your way through the code. Consider collapsing all the method bodies to give you a smaller surface area to peruse (see Figure 2-4). Alternatively, many IDEs can show you an outline of a given class, providing a higher-level view of the code. Read the method names. What does that tell you about the purpose of the module?

用你的集成开发环境（IDE）来导航代码。许多 IDE 能让你在阅读代码时轻松跳转到其他类的方法（见图 2-3）。可以考虑把所有方法体折叠起来，给你一块更小、更易浏览的区域（见图 2-4）。或者，许多 IDE 还能展示某个类的大纲，给你一个更高层的代码视图。读一读方法名——它们告诉你这个模块是干什么的？

Do not assume the code does what the name implies. As code evolves, variable and method names may no longer reflect reality. Don’t rush; confirm your hunches. Resist the temptation to cut corners and potentially create more work later on. In other words, take the time it takes, so it takes less time.

不要想当然地认为代码做的就是名字所暗示的事。随着代码演进，变量名和方法名可能早已名不副实。别急；验证你的直觉。别图省事走捷径，免得日后制造更多麻烦。换句话说，该花的时间花到位，往后花的时间才会更少。

Exceptions can mislead. More than once, we have encountered exceptions that made incorrect assumptions about possible error conditions. Pay extra care to situations that catch very high-level exceptions; while expedient for the author, they tend to obfuscate the possible problems.

异常也会误导人。我们不止一次遇到过对可能错误情形做出错误假设的异常。对那些捕获非常高层异常的情况要格外小心；虽然对作者来说图了省事，却往往把真正可能的问题掩盖掉。

Your IDE may also include tools or plug-ins that help you analyze the code. For example, IntelliJ IDEA can quickly show you dependencies, giving you a sense of how the code works together (see Figure 2-5). Modern developer tools are powerful; let them help you understand the code.

你的 IDE 可能还附带帮你分析代码的工具或插件。例如，IntelliJ IDEA 能快速展示依赖关系，让你感受代码是如何协作的（见图 2-5）。现代开发者工具很强大；让它们帮你理解代码。

Use your source code management tool as well (see Figure 2-6). Many modern tools allow you to quickly move about your project. Look at the change history of the files. What changes frequently? What do the commit logs tell you about the updates? Start with the most frequently modified classes, something Git can show you with a command like this:

  | sort | uniq -c | sort -rg | head -10

Your IDE can also show you the change history if you don’t feel like using the command line. However you choose to investigate the code, don’t be afraid to reach out to your teammates with questions!

你还可以用 git blame 之类的工具把代码的修改可视化。如果你刚加入一个新项目，团队里谁做了最近的修改、谁改得最频繁？如果你不想用命令行，IDE 也能展示变更历史。无论你选择怎么调查代码，都别害怕带着问题去找队友！

While purpose-built project models often fall out of sync with the code as the application evolves, you can always extract diagrams from the codebase. Effective Code-Reading Strategies

Now that you have a grasp on the project’s purpose and a good lay of the land, it’s time to start understanding the code. In this section, you will learn some effective strategies for reading code, such as leveraging IDE features and analyzing tests for insight.

既然你已经掌握了项目的目的、也摸清了大致地形，就该开始理解代码了。本节你将学到一些高效读代码的策略，比如善用 IDE 特性、通过分析测试获取洞见。

Leveraging IDE Features

Your IDE is so much more than a text editor for writing code. IDEs have a wide range of features that can help you write, debug, and navigate codebases with ease. When working with existing code, your IDE becomes even more valuable as a tool for exploration and comprehension.

你的 IDE 远不止是一个写代码的文本编辑器。它有丰富的特性，能帮你轻松地编写、调试和导航代码库。当你与既有代码打交道时，IDE 作为探索和理解工具的价值会进一步放大。

原书第 49 页

Continuous learning approach. IDEs are so powerful these days that it would be almost impossible to figure out every little trick they have. Instead, you should focus on learning something new every week. For example, JetBrains IntelliJ IDEA is a favorite among Java developers, and it has a really nice feature called the Tip of the Day. When you open up the IDE, there is a tip to help you get acquainted with the features.

持续学习的心态。如今的 IDE 强大到几乎不可能把每个小窍门都摸清楚。因此你应当专注于每周学一点新东西。例如，JetBrains IntelliJ IDEA 是 Java 开发者的宠儿，它有一个非常贴心的功能叫“每日提示”。每次打开 IDE，都会弹出一条小提示，帮你熟悉各种特性。

These tips cover everything from shortcuts, tools, refactoring, debugging, and plug-ins. Learning the shortcuts of your IDE will make you a much more productive developer, and this is the first place you should start. You will find similar features in a lot of the IDEs on the market today, so check the documentation and start learning. If you happen to miss the tip of the day in IntelliJ, you can always find it by choosing Help → Tip of the day. In the tip shown in Figure 2-8, IntelliJ is teaching us about a feature called live templates, which can be used to insert frequent code constructs.

这些提示涵盖快捷键、工具、重构、调试和插件等方方面面。学会 IDE 的快捷键会让你高效得多，这也是你应当最先入手的地方。如今市面上很多 IDE 都有类似功能，所以翻翻文档开始学吧。如果你错过了 IntelliJ 的每日提示，随时可以通过帮助 → 每日提示找回来。在图 2-8 所示的提示里，IntelliJ 正在教我们一个叫“实时模板”的功能，用来快速插入常用的代码结构。

建一份个人 IDE 技巧文档，把你发现的新快捷键或新特性记下来。定期回顾，巩固所学。时常翻看这份文档，用你记下的技巧练就肌肉记忆。

Code navigation tools. One of the most valuable skills when exploring an unfamiliar codebase is the ability to navigate efficiently through the code. Many IDEs will allow you to jump to and even create code in other files without having to manually open up that file through the navigation bar. In the following sections, you will find some practical navigation features that can dramatically speed up your code exploration.

代码导航工具。探索陌生代码库时，最有价值的技能之一就是高效地在代码间穿梭。许多 IDE 能让你跳转到其他文件、甚至在那里直接创建代码，而不用手动通过导航栏打开那个文件。接下来你会看到一些实用的导航特性，能大幅加快你的代码探索速度。

Find usages and references. When you’re trying to understand a class or a component, you need to see where in the codebase it is being used. Modern IDEs excel at this task, and it’s something you should get familiar with. If you were to open up a Java interface in IntelliJ, such as the one shown in Figure 2-9, you can click the gutter icon to find all implementations of that interface.8 This is really handy when you’re trying to understand how an abstraction is used in practice. Similarly, you can right-click a method name and select Find Usages to see every place where that method is called.

查找用法与引用。当你试图理解一个类或组件时，你需要看到它在代码库的哪些地方被使用。现代 IDE 非常擅长这件事，你应当熟悉它。如果你在 IntelliJ 里打开一个 Java 接口（如图 2-9 所示），可以点击 gutter 图标找到该接口的所有实现类。8当你想理解一个抽象在实践中是怎么被使用时，这特别方便。同样，你可以右键一个方法名，选“查找用法”，看到这个方法被调用的每一处。

8 A Java interface is a reference type that defines a contract of methods that implementing classes must provide, allowing for abstraction and polymorphism in Java programs.
Java 接口是一种引用类型，它定义了一组方法契约，实现类必须提供这些方法，从而在 Java 程序中实现抽象与多态。

Jump to definition. Another useful IDE navigation feature is the ability to jump to the definition of a class, method, or variable. This lets you quickly move from usage to implementation, following the code’s logical flow. For example, if you’re writing a Java application and using an ArrayList and want to learn how it works, you can Command-click (or Ctrl-click on Windows/Linux) on the ArrayList type to be taken to the source, where you can view the code and documentation for that type (see Figure 2-10).

跳转到定义。另一个有用的 IDE 导航特性是跳转到类、方法或变量的定义。这能让你沿代码的逻辑流，从使用处快速跳到实现处。例如，如果你在写一个 Java 应用、用到了 ArrayList 并想了解它是怎么工作的，可以 Command+点击（Windows/Linux 上是 Ctrl+点击）ArrayList 类型，就会跳到源码，在那里查看该类型的代码和文档（见图 2-10）。

The ability to jump to a definition is valuable when working with the following:

跳转到定义的能力，在处理以下内容时格外有价值：

  • Third-party libraries第三方库
  • Framework code框架代码
  • Base classes and interfaces基类与接口
  • Utility methods used throughout the codebase整个代码库都在使用的工具方法

Call hierarchies and dependency views. Understanding how components interact is crucial to grasping an unfamiliar codebase. IDEs offer specialized views for visualizing these relationships:

调用层级与依赖视图。理解组件之间如何交互，是掌握陌生代码库的关键。IDE 提供专门的视图来可视化这些关系：

  • Call hierarchy — shows what calls a method and what methods it calls调用层级——显示谁调用了这个方法，以及这个方法调用了哪些方法
  • Type hierarchy — displays inheritance relationships类型层级——展示继承关系
  • Dependency diagram — visualizes how modules or packages depend on each other依赖图——可视化模块或包之间如何相互依赖

For example, in IntelliJ, you can right-click a method and select Show Call Hierarchy to see both incoming calls (where this method is called from) and outgoing calls (methods this method calls). This can quickly show you a method’s role in the larger system.

例如在 IntelliJ 中，你可以右键一个方法，选“显示调用层级”，同时看到入站调用（这个方法被谁调用）和出站调用（这个方法调用了谁）。这能让你快速看清一个方法在更大系统中扮演的角色。

Code analysis features. Modern IDEs have powerful tools to help you navigate code, but they can do so much more. They can actively analyze the code that you’re writing and offer insights that can both improve your code and help you learn new features you might not have been aware of.

代码分析特性。现代 IDE 除了帮你导航代码，还能做更多。它们会主动分析你正在写的代码，给出洞见，既能改进代码，又能帮你学到自己可能没意识到的新特性。

Automated inspection and suggestions. When you write or modify code, IDEs can offer suggestions on how to refactor code. It’s important to remember that these are merely suggestions: you don’t always have to accept them, but it is helpful to review them. These suggestions often reveal common patterns and best practices that can not only improve code quality but also teach you something new in the process.

自动检查与建议。当你编写或修改代码时，IDE 会给出如何重构的建议。要记住：这些只是建议，你不必照单全收，但过一遍很有好处。这些建议往往揭示了常见模式和最佳实践，既能提升代码质量，也能在过程中教你新东西。

Here’s an example in Java where the code is iterating over a collection of Books. For each Book in the collection, the code simply prints out the name of the book:

下面是一个 Java 例子：代码遍历一个 Book 集合，对集合里的每本书，简单地打印书名：

List<Book> books = library.getBooks();
for (Book book : books) {
    System.out.println(book.getTitle());
}

This works, and there is nothing wrong with the code, but IntelliJ might suggest using a more streamlined approach:

这能跑，代码也没毛病，但 IntelliJ 可能会建议用更精简的写法：

library.getBooks().forEach(book -> System.out.println(book.getTitle()));

These suggestions not only help you write better code but also teach you idiomatic patterns in the language and frameworks you’re using.

这些建议不仅帮你写出更好的代码，还教你所用语言和框架的惯用法。

Code structure visualization. Another important part of being able to effectively read code is understanding how the code is structured within a project or even a single class. IDEs often include features that visualize the structure of your code. If you want to try to understand how the code in Figure 2-11 is architected, for example, you can look in the project structure and quickly see that it is a monolithic application and the code is organized in a package-by-feature arrangement.

代码结构可视化。高效阅读代码的另一项关键，是理解代码在一个项目乃至单个类内部是如何组织的。IDE 通常有把代码结构可视化的特性。例如，如果你想理解图 2-11 中的代码是怎么架构的，可以看看项目结构，很快就能发现这是一个单体应用，代码是按“一个特性一个包”的方式组织的。

Suppose you were trying to understand what methods were available in a certain class. Sure, you could check out the API documentation, but do you even know if that is the most up-to-date version of the docs? You could manually open up a class file and begin scrolling through the source code, but this could take some time. Most IDEs have a way to visualize the structure of a class or component. In the example shown in Figure 2-12, you are looking at the structure of the OwnerController in a project called PetClinic. You can see at a glance what methods are available in the class, giving you quick insights into the purpose of this class and its functionality.

假设你想了解某个类里有哪些方法。当然，你可以查 API 文档，但你怎么知道那是最新版文档？你也可以手动打开类文件、从头翻源码，但这可能要花不少时间。大多数 IDE 都有办法把一个类或组件的结构可视化。在图 2-12 的例子里，你看到的是 PetClinic 项目中 OwnerController 的结构。一眼就能看出这个类有哪些方法，从而迅速理解这个类的用途和功能。

Reading Tests for Insight

When it comes to exploring a new codebase, tests serve as another form of documentation for developers. Well-written tests reveal not only what the code does but also why it does it a certain way. While the code will tell you how something works, tests will tell you how it’s supposed to work.

探索新代码库时，测试是给开发者看的另一种文档。写得好的测试不仅揭示代码做了什么，还揭示它为什么这么做。代码会告诉你某样东西是怎么工作的，而测试会告诉你它本该怎么工作。

Tests as living documentation. Unlike traditional documentation that often becomes outdated, tests must remain functional to pass continuous integration checks. This makes them a reliable, up-to-date source of truth about system behavior.

测试是活文档。传统文档常常会过时，但测试必须保持可运行才能通过持续集成检查。这使它们成为关于系统行为的、可靠且最新的事实来源。

Tests document the expected inputs and outputs of methods, the interactions between components, and the overall system behavior. By reading tests first, you can understand what a component is supposed to do before diving into how it actually does it. This provides crucial context that makes the implementation easier to comprehend.

测试记录了方法的预期输入输出、组件之间的交互以及整体系统行为。先读测试，你就能在一头扎进“它怎么实现”之前，先理解“这个组件本该做什么”。这提供了关键上下文，让实现更容易读懂。

The following test verifies that regular customers receive a 10% bulk discount when placing large orders over a certain threshold, ensuring that the pricing service correctly calculates discounts based on order size rather than customer type:

下面这个测试验证：当普通客户下超过某个门槛的大订单时，会获得 10% 的批量折扣；从而确保定价服务是按订单金额、而不是按客户类型来正确计算折扣的：

原书第 55 页
@Test
public void shouldApplyBulkDiscountForLargeOrders() {
    // Given
    Customer regularCustomer = new Customer(CustomerType.REGULAR);
    Order bulkOrder = new Order(regularCustomer, 500.00);

    // When
    double finalPrice = pricingService.calculateFinalPrice(bulkOrder);

    // Assert
    assertEquals(450.00, finalPrice, 0.01);
}

With that context, you can now dive into the pricing service class and examine the calculateFinalPrice method to understand the code that produces that result.

有了这段上下文，你就可以钻进定价服务类，查看 calculateFinalPrice 方法，理解产生这个结果的代码。

Understanding workflows and processes. Tests can often map to user stories, which often make them a great way of understanding business processes or workflows. If you zoom out and look at integration tests, they can often show you the big picture of how components work together to fulfill business requirements.

理解工作流与业务流程。测试往往能映射到用户故事，这使它们成为理解业务流程或工作流的绝佳途径。如果你拉远视角看集成测试，它们常常能展示组件如何协作满足业务需求的全貌。

Look for tests that verify entire processes from start to finish. These tests often contain setup code that represents real-world scenarios, giving you context about how the system behaves in production.

寻找那些端到端验证整个流程的测试。这些测试往往包含代表真实场景的搭建代码，让你了解系统在生产环境中是怎么表现的。

The following test verifies that when a user submits a product review, the review service correctly updates the product’s average rating and sends a notification to the administrator, ensuring both the data persistence and notification aspects of the review process work as expected:

下面这个测试验证：当用户提交一条产品评价时，评价服务会正确更新产品的平均评分，并向管理员发送通知；从而确保评价流程的数据持久化和通知两方面都按预期工作：

@Test
public void submitProductReviewShouldUpdateRatingAndNotifyAdmin() {
    // Given
    Product product = productService.findProductById("XYZ789");
    User user = userService.findByUsername("janedoe");
    Review review = new Review(user, product, 4, "Great quality product!");

    // When
    ReviewResult result = reviewService.submitReview(review);

    // Then
    assertTrue(result.isSuccessful());
    assertEquals(4.2, productService.findProductById("XYZ789")
    .getAverageRating(), 0.01);
    verify(notificationService).sendReviewNotification(anyObject(), eq("XYZ789"));
}

With this context, you now understand the whole flow of what happens when a user submits a new review.

有了这段上下文，你就理解了用户提交一条新评价时的完整流程。

原书第 56 页

Discovering edge cases and boundaries. In software development, an edge case is a situation that occurs at the extreme edge of a program’s expected input, operating conditions, or usage patterns, and is often the case where assumptions break down. These inputs or conditions are valid but unusual, and they will reveal bugs that don’t typically happen during the “typical” or “happy-path” scenarios. In existing codebases, you might find more tests around these because they were discovered over time, and a test was written to ensure they don’t surface again.

发现边界情况与边界条件。在软件开发中，边界情况是指发生在程序预期输入、运行条件或使用模式极端边缘的情形，往往正是假设失效的地方。这些输入或条件是合法但不常见的，它们会暴露出在“典型”或“快乐路径”场景下通常不会出现的 bug。在既有代码库里，你会发现围绕这些情况的测试往往更多，因为它们是在长期使用中被发现的，于是写了个测试确保不再重现。

Pay special attention to tests with names like shouldHandleEmptyList, shouldRejectInvalidInput, or shouldTimeoutAfterTenSeconds. These tests show you the limits of the system’s capabilities and highlight potential failure points.

特别注意那些命名像 shouldHandleEmptyList、shouldRejectInvalidInput 或 shouldTimeoutAfterTenSeconds 的测试。它们向你展示系统能力的边界，标出潜在的失败点。

The following test reveals that the system will handle expired credit cards and fail gracefully. This is something that might not be as obvious if you were just reading through the implementation:

下面这个测试揭示：系统会处理过期信用卡并优雅地失败。如果你只是通读实现，这一点可能不会这么明显：

@Test
public void shouldRejectPaymentWhenCreditCardIsExpired() {
    // Given
    CreditCard expiredCard = new CreditCard("4111111111111111", "05/20");
    Order order = new Order(new Customer(), 50.00);

    // When
    PaymentResult result = paymentService.processPayment(order, expiredCard);

    // Then
    assertFalse(result.isSuccessful());
    assertEquals(PaymentFailureReason.EXPIRED_CARD, result.getFailureReason());
}

With this context, you can go through the implementation of the process payment method and look for the functionality that will catch this edge case.

有了这段上下文，你就可以通读 processPayment 方法的实现，找到处理这个边界情况的代码。

With the ability to understand a project and effectively read code, it’s time to modify the code. But how can you go about doing that safely? We’ll cover that topic in the next section.

具备了理解项目和高效读代码的能力，就该动手改代码了。但怎样才能安全地改？下一节我们会讲这个话题。

Practice Makes Perfect

At the end of the day, practice some grace with yourself. Modern codebases are often sprawling. One person cannot understand it in its entirety, and that isn’t the goal. Your knowledge will grow over time. Rinse and repeat the process as you encounter new parts of your project. It can be intimidating, but every developer has gone through it. You will be fine!

说到底，对自己宽容一点。现代代码库往往庞杂庞大。一个人不可能全部理解，那也不是目标。你的知识会随时间增长。遇到项目里新的部分，就把这个过程重复一遍。这可能令人畏惧，但每个开发者都经历过。你会没事的！

原书第 57 页

How do you improve your code-reading skills? As much as you may dread it, practice reading code. There are so many well-written, publicly available, open source options in a variety of languages for you to choose from. There aren’t any shortcuts; you cannot improve without practice. It does get easier over time, and you will get faster.

怎么提高读代码的能力？尽管你可能不想听，但答案就是：多读代码。有大量写得很好、公开可得、各种语言的开源项目供你选择。没有捷径；不练习就不会进步。不过它确实会越来越容易，你也会越读越快。

What About AI?
那 AI 呢？

Like any discipline, software tooling continues to evolve. From shell-based text editors to IDEs with integrated refactoring tools and IntelliSense code completion, writing code has gotten easier. Of course, the size and complexity of the applications you’re working on has also grown, so perhaps it’s a wash! With the advent of things like GitHub Copilot and generative AI like ChatGPT, some have even suggested that developers will soon be replaced. The rumors of the end of developers are often grossly exaggerated, from COBOL to fourth-generation programming languages to various drag-and-drop “programming” solutions failing to result in a large-scale reduction in the demand for software engineering.
和任何学科一样，软件工具也在持续演进。从基于 shell 的文本编辑器，到带集成重构工具和 IntelliSense 补全的 IDE，写代码变得越来越容易。当然，你所面对应用的规模和复杂度也在增长，所以也许算是扯平了！随着 GitHub Copilot 这类工具、以及 ChatGPT 这类生成式 AI 的出现，有人甚至预言开发者很快会被取代。但“开发者末日”的传闻一向被大大夸大：从 COBOL，到第四代编程语言，再到各种拖拽式“编程”方案，都没有导致软件工程需求的大规模减少。
These tools have a place in your toolbox—for example, you can ask ChatGPT what a chunk of code does,9 but you still need to understand the context. AI doesn’t know the purpose of a given class, so you still need to read the code, wade through the documentation, and talk to your fellow developers. AI doesn’t (yet) fully understand an entire enterprise codebase, and the risk of hallucinations is real. While AI can help you, ultimately, you must understand the nuance and relationships between code spread across multiple repositories.
这些工具在你的工具箱里有一席之地——比如你可以问 ChatGPT 一段代码是干什么的，9但你仍然需要理解上下文。AI 并不知道某个类的目的，所以你还是得读代码、啃文档、和同事交流。AI （目前）并不能完全理解整个企业级代码库，幻觉的风险真实存在。AI 能帮你，但归根结底，分散在多个仓库里的代码之间的细微差别和关系，必须由你来理解。
As Dan likes to say, when using AI, you are the pilot, not the passenger: trust but verify. AI can understand code in a vacuum, but it may not understand an enterprise-grade codebase without possible hallucinations. Modern applications are often spread across many repositories, leveraging multiple libraries. You, the developer, must understand the relationships and intricacies in order to enable the AI tools to be successful in accelerating development.
正如 Dan 常说的：用 AI 的时候，你是飞行员，不是乘客——信任但要核实。AI 能在真空中理解代码，但它未必能不带幻觉地理解一个企业级代码库。现代应用往往分散在多个仓库、依赖多个库。你——作为开发者——必须理解其中的关系和错综复杂之处，才能让 AI 工具真正有效地加速开发。
9 Your organization’s lawyers likely have strong opinions about the use of such tools, so double-check your corporate policies before you paste your proprietary pricing algorithm into a model that might be using your code as training data!
你们公司法务对这类工具的使用很可能有强硬意见；在把自家专有的定价算法粘贴进某个可能拿你的代码当训练数据的模型之前，务必再核对一遍公司政策！

Wrapping Up

Arguably, coding is taught backward: you learn to write before you learn to read, and yet you will spend a significant amount of your career reading code written by someone else. While you may not enjoy existing code as much as greenfield development, it comes with the paycheck. Rather than run from the situation, learn to embrace it, as there is much to gain professionally. Be aware of cognitive biases.

可以说，编程被教反了：你先学写、后学读，可职业生涯中你却要花大量时间读别人写的代码。虽然你可能不像喜欢绿地开发那样喜欢既有代码，但薪水就是为它付的。与其逃避，不如学会拥抱它，因为专业上你会收获良多。警惕认知偏见。

原书第 58 页

Don’t be afraid to roll up your sleeves and root around in an unfamiliar codebase; you will learn something. As your understanding grows, leave the code better than you found it, easing the path of the next developer—which just might be you!

别害怕卷起袖子在陌生代码库里刨一刨；你一定会学到东西。随着理解加深，把代码改得比你发现它时更好，为下一位开发者铺平道路——而那个人很可能就是你自己！

Putting It into Practice

If you want to get better at reading code, there are no shortcuts; you need to read more code. Luckily, you have a veritable plethora of open source projects at your disposal! Block out a couple of hours to read some of the code in the framework you use (or the one you wish you used) at work or in another project you’re interested in. If you’re not sure where to start, check out the trending repositories on GitHub. Apply the techniques you learned in this chapter. In a couple of months, pick another part of the project you explored or try a completely different one; was it easier than the first time? Keep at it; over time, your code-reading skills will improve.

想提高读代码的能力，没有捷径；你需要读更多代码。幸运的是，你手边有浩如烟海的开源项目！抽出两小时，读一读你工作中用的（或希望自己用的）框架代码，或者你感兴趣的另一个项目。不知道从哪开始？去看看 GitHub 上的热门仓库。运用你在本章学到的技巧。几个月后，再挑你看过的项目的另一部分，或者试一个完全不同的项目；是不是比第一次轻松了？坚持下去，你的读码能力会不断提高。

Working with existing code is also a skill that needs to be developed, and once again, open source software gives you a massive playground to explore. Contributing to open source is an excellent learning laboratory, and it isn’t nearly as hard to get started as you may think.10 Pick a project and spend a few hours working with it.

与既有代码打交道也是一项需要培养的技能，而开源软件再次给了你一个巨大的游乐场。为开源做贡献是极好的学习实验室，而且入门远没有你想象的那么难。10挑一个项目，花几个小时和它互动吧。

10 Many projects have lists of bugs marked as “for first-time contributors,” but don’t be afraid to reach out to the current project contributors; most will happily help you get up and running.
许多项目都有标记为“适合首次贡献者”的 bug 清单；也别害怕联系当前项目的贡献者，大多数人会很乐意帮你跑起来。
